decision_question: Is the product ready for public release within its explicitly stated scope as a neutral, citation-first scripture reference and comparative-literacy SPA?
acceptance_criteria: Public claims match observable implementation and traceable sources.
The four core workflows serve their stated audiences.
Attribution, licensing, canon and denomination limits, and provider failure boundaries are clear.
Neutrality, safety, privacy, and portability boundaries are credible.
Quality evidence is repeatable enough to support the product's public claims.

shared_model_or_source_limits: All initial reviewers inspected the same repository commit and origin archive.
Reviewer model family was shared and results are therefore correlated.
The review was analytical; no external holdout or specialist audit was used.

material_findings: Demographic scope claims lack exact report, table, denominator, and extraction provenance.
Orthodox and LDS coverage is represented more strongly than the available editions and fallbacks support.
The advertised Sefaria bilingual option was not routed through the bilingual adapter.
CI and lint do not yet provide complete repeatable evidence for public claims.
Browse, exact lookup, seeded comparison, and observance workflows are substantially implemented.
Paraphrase discovery, ambiguity handling, commentary-level control, and broad translation comparison remain absent or partial.
Partial/fallback provider paths need stronger point-of-use communication.
The reference UI has no chat-style hostile-prompt surface, but its original refusal behavior is not implemented as a public contract.
GitHub Pages subpath assets and direct-route behavior need production verification.
Accessibility and stale-request behavior lack automated release evidence.

falsification_hypotheses: Sefaria bilingual selection may return English-only text.
A production deep link may load without correct subpath assets or metadata.
A slower earlier lookup response may overwrite a newer request.
Orthodox users may infer complete edition coverage from a partial data path.
Keyboard and 200-percent zoom users may lose essential lookup or calendar state.
The declared lint command may fail from a clean install.

test_results.note: Requires deterministic API and UI test harness.
Requires a production-path Pages smoke test.
The misleading full-coverage label was replaced with explicit partial-coverage wording.
Requires automated accessibility and keyboard matrix.
Lint now runs successfully after adding compatible ESLint/Babel tooling.

decisive_evidence: The core routes exist and live provider smoke tests passed for the current provider set.
The repository and independent reviews identify blocked claims that cannot be supported by current automated evidence.
Coverage and translation wording defects are material because they change what users believe they are reading.
unresolved_items: Exact demographic provenance and denominator compatibility.
Complete production deep-link and subpath asset behavior.
Automated accessibility, routing, race, and provider-contract coverage.
Whether bounded paraphrase discovery and context levels remain committed product requirements.

limitations: Exact-reference lookup is supported; fuzzy/paraphrase discovery is not yet a release capability.
Christian denominational coverage is uneven and Orthodox/LDS paths are partial or community/static fallbacks.
Public-provider availability and data freshness remain external dependencies.
No unrestricted claim of full canon, translation, commentary, accessibility, or scholarly coverage is supported.
This is not theological, legal, accessibility-certification, security, or other specialist authority.
follow_up: Add deterministic provider/provenance, routing, state, and accessibility tests.
Verify GitHub Pages production paths and assets.
Reconcile exact demographic sources and point-of-use scope copy.
Decide and implement or explicitly retire paraphrase and commentary-level requirements.
Re-run the equilibrium review after the release candidate is frozen.
